skill.name: agent-speedup-estimator
skill.description: Scan local Claude Code and Codex transcripts to measure how long agent runs spend on model time versus local tool time (builds, tests, installs, scripts), then estimate how much faster they would run on a new computer. Use when the user asks whether their computer is slowing their coding agents, whether to upgrade or buy a new laptop or desktop, or how much faster a specific chip would make Claude Code or Codex. 中文触发：电脑是不是拖慢了 agent、要不要换新电脑、换电脑能快多少。
skill.summary: Measure local tool time, model time, and hardware-related speedup for Claude Code and Codex runs.
skill.author: hnewcity

security_audit.summary: Confirmed findings are limited to intentional access to hidden Claude Code and Codex transcript directories, which may expose sensitive local history to the skill. The remaining alerts are false positives for static URLs, documentation syntax, report JavaScript, hardware probes, test fixtures, and structured catalog data; no prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found. Static review was capped at 400/3390 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 2990 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Local transcripts can contain private prompts, replies, commands, and project paths.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent, limit reads to selected directories, and document retention and report-sharing controls.

remediation.issue: Transcript parsing assumes local files are trusted input.
remediation.suggestion: Keep parsing local, avoid writing raw records, and add tests that assert prompts, replies, commands, and session paths never enter reports.

remediation.issue: CPU source URLs are static references and may become stale.
remediation.suggestion: Pin source dates and review catalog provenance before publishing new score data.

content.user_title: Measure Agent Speedups on a Faster Computer
content.value_statement: Slow local builds, tests, and installs can make coding agents feel unresponsive. This skill separates remote model time from local tool time and estimates hardware-related speedup ranges.
actual_capabilities: Parse local Claude Code and Codex timing records without copying prompts or replies into reports.
Separate model time from local tool time across builds, tests, installs, scripts, and other command categories.
Estimate speedup ranges for cataloged CPUs and named target machines using Geekbench 6 references.
Detect current hardware and disk class to establish a baseline.
Generate Markdown, HTML, and JSON reports with assumptions, ranges, and saved-time estimates.
Support English and Chinese report output.
limitations: Estimates use sensitivity assumptions, not direct benchmarks of every workload.
Remote model time does not improve with local hardware.
Local models, remote builds, GPUs, memory upgrades, and network overhead are outside the model.
Results depend on available transcript timing records and CPU score coverage.

use_cases.title: Audit a personal workstation
use_cases.description: Measure how much of your agent work is local and estimate whether a faster computer could reduce waiting time.

use_cases.title: Plan a team hardware refresh
use_cases.description: Use aggregate timing reports to compare likely gains before standardizing a new developer machine.

use_cases.title: Compare a named target machine
use_cases.description: Evaluate a specific laptop or desktop against the current system with documented CPU score assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Get a baseline report
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my available Claude Code and Codex history. Separate model time from local tool time and summarize the main sources of delay.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two target machines
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my current computer with [target one] and [target two]. Show expected speedup ranges, hours saved, and the assumptions behind each estimate.

prompt_templates.title: Review a recent period
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the last [number] days of agent activity. Focus on builds, tests, installs, and scripts, then explain which local categories benefit most from a hardware upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Calibrate with measured scores
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my measured Geekbench 6 single-core score of [single] and multi-core score of [multi] as the current baseline. Compare it with [exact target] and state all uncertainty sources.

output_examples.input: I want to know whether my laptop slows down Claude Code.
output_examples.output: The report separates remote model time from local tool time, then estimates the speedup available from faster CPU and disk hardware.

output_examples.input: Compare my current computer with an Apple M4 Pro over the last 30 days.
output: Expected gains are limited when most time is spent waiting for the remote model.
Builds, tests, and installs receive the largest hardware-related benefit.
The report shows conservative, expected, and optimistic ranges.

output_examples.input: Use my measured CPU scores instead of an inferred baseline.
output_examples.output: The estimate uses the supplied scores, labels the baseline as measured, and preserves uncertainty from workload sensitivity assumptions.

best_practices: Name an exact target CPU or machine when comparing hardware.
Read the assumptions and ranges before treating a result as a purchase decision.
Keep transcript directories and generated reports private because local history can contain sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a CPU score comparison as a benchmark of your complete workload.
Do not share raw transcripts or reports without reviewing activity dates and hardware details.
Do not compare Geekbench scores from different major versions as if they were equivalent.

faq.question: Does this measure model response speed?
faq.answer: It estimates model time from local timing records, but remote model inference is treated as unchanged by your computer.

faq.question: What data does the skill read?
faq.answer: It reads local Claude Code and Codex timing records, hardware metadata, and bundled CPU reference data.

faq.question: Are prompts and replies included in reports?
faq.answer: The skill is designed to exclude prompts, replies, raw commands, transcript paths, and session identifiers from reports.

faq.question: Can I compare a specific laptop or desktop?
faq.answer: Yes. Use an exact catalog name when available, and review whether the estimate uses measured scores, a stand-in, or a fallback.

faq.question: Are the speedup numbers guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. They are scenario ranges based on CPU scores and sensitivity assumptions, not guarantees or full workload benchmarks.

faq.question: Does it support both Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It has adapters for both tools and reports where usable timing records are available.
